body.title: govern audit sync fails with "Too many total parameters" for long sessions
body.description:
`glab govern audit sync` batches audit events by count only (500 per request), but GitLab limits that endpoint to 5,000 JSON elements, and one event is 13 to 25 or more. So a session with more than about 200 events to upload fails with:

```plaintext
could not post audit events: could not post audit events: POST https://gitlab.com/api/v4/projects/<id>/ai_agent/audit_events: 400 {error: Too many total parameters}
```

The cursor doesn't move on failure, so every later sync sends the same batch and the session never finishes syncing. The error prefix is also repeated.

GitLab is raising the limit in https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/263119, but older self-managed versions keep 5,000, so glab needs to batch by size too.

Details and the customer report: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/634442

body.title: feat: report pipeline status via OSC 7501 in `ci status --live`
body.description:
### Problem to solve

As a developer running `glab ci status --live` or `glab ci status --wait`, I want my terminal tab to show whether the pipeline is still running, has passed, or has failed, so I can switch to other work without repeatedly checking the tab.

### Proposal

Report pipeline state from `glab ci status --live` / `--wait` using the [Program Status Protocol (OSC 7501)](https://github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea/releases), which recent Bubble Tea releases support:

| Pipeline state | Program status | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `created`, `pending`, `running` | working | e.g. `pipeline #123 running (4/12 jobs)` |
| `success` | finished | `pipeline #123 passed` |
| `failed` | failed | e.g. `job rspec 3/8 failed` |
| `canceled`, `skipped` | finished/failed | pipeline status |
| `manual` (blocked) | waiting on user | `pipeline #123 waiting on manual job` |

Implementation notes:

- `ci status` renders through `uilive`, not a `tea.Program`, so add a small helper in `internal/iostreams` (for example `SetProgramStatus(state, reason)`) that writes the sequence directly.
- Emit only when output is a TTY. Never emit for `--output json`, piped output, or `GITLAB_CI`.
- Reset the status on exit, including Ctrl+C, so a stale "working" indicator isn't left behind.
- Consider an opt-out (config key in `KeySchema` or env var) while terminal support is new.

### Further details

Once the helper exists, other long-running or interactive commands can reuse it in follow-ups: `ci trace`, `mr merge` waiting on pipelines, `auth login`, `stack sync` conflicts, `duo ask`, and the shared `Confirm`/`Input`/`Select` prompts and spinner.

### Links / references

- Bubble Tea release announcing OSC 7501 support
- `internal/commands/ci/status/status.go`

body.title: Terminal background-colour query blocks every TTY command, up to 5s per query
body.description:
## Summary

When stdout is a terminal, every glab command blocks on a terminal background-colour query (an OSC 11 request that waits for the terminal's reply).

- `NewCmdRoot` (`internal/commands/root.go:64`) calls `f.IO().Color()` eagerly, only to colour one help string.
- `Color()` runs `termenv.HasDarkBackground()` (`internal/iostreams/color.go:55`), which waits for the terminal to answer. Nothing caches the result, so the query runs again on every `Color()` call.
- `termenv.HasDarkBackground()` is also called directly in `internal/iostreams/iostreams.go:373` and `internal/commands/help/help.go:31`.
- fang runs its own query on help and error output.

Result: 1 query for `glab version`, and 2 for `mr list`, `issue list` and `--help`.

## Impact

- Local terminal: about zero.
- Over SSH at 50ms RTT: adds 50–100ms per command.
- A terminal that never answers waits out `termenv.OSCTimeout` (5s) on each query: about 5s for `version` and 9s for `--help`.
- Setting `glamour_style` or `GLAB_GLAMOUR_STYLE=dark` does not skip the query. Only `NO_COLOR` does.

## Proposal

1. Drop the eager `Color()` call in `NewCmdRoot`, and colour the help string lazily.
2. Detect the background once per process and reuse the result in all call sites (`color.go`, `iostreams.go`, `help/help.go`).
3. Honour an explicit style (`glamour_style` / `GLAB_GLAMOUR_STYLE` set to `dark` or `light`) before probing the terminal.
4. Lower `termenv.OSCTimeout` from its 5s default.
5. Upstream: ask fang for an option to accept a known dark/light value, so it doesn't run its own query.

## Acceptance criteria

- At most one background query per process, and none when the style is set explicitly or `NO_COLOR` is set.
- A terminal that never answers does not delay commands by seconds.

Found during review of https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/4139. Related: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/work_items/8626 (telemetry blocks exit).
